# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Member:** Taylor Foster
**Member ID:** W492196775
**Payer/Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Wyoming
**Denial date:** 2026-08-24
**Reference number:** POC-C65CA65DA3-33163
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0736 - Hip Preservation Surgery (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0736.html), last review 07/31/2026

---

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), referenced above. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Aetna to reconsider its decision.

## Why I believe this denial should be reversed

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to walk through what the record actually shows, alongside the plan's own language.

I should note up front that the policy excerpts I have been given are drawn from Aetna CPB 0736 - Hip Preservation Surgery, and most of the specific numbered criteria in that policy address other procedures — pelvic osteotomy, iliopsoas tenotomy after hip replacement, and gluteus medius tears — rather than hip arthroscopy for labral tear and femoroacetabular impingement specifically. I am not able to quote a provision from that policy that is written specifically for arthroscopic treatment of a labral tear with cam impingement, because I have not seen one. I want to be transparent about that rather than overstate what the policy says.

That said, the same policy does set out a general benchmark for how long symptoms should be present before hip preservation surgery is considered, stating:

> "and Minimum 6 months of symptoms;"

My symptoms have been present far longer than that. The clinical summary documents 24 months of progressive hip pain that has not improved with rest.

In addition, I completed a substantial course of conservative treatment before surgery was recommended:

- **Physical therapy:** 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 18 visits completed between 2026-04-27 and 2026-08-03, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** 8 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-14, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

Despite this treatment, I continue to have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I am unable to run or squat. On exam, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion. My MRI arthrogram from 2026-07-11 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement (alpha angle 68 degrees), with joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0.

Given the length of time I have had symptoms, and the extent of physical therapy, medication, and injection treatment I have already tried without lasting improvement, I do not believe it is accurate to say I have not had an adequate trial of conservative care. I am asking Aetna to look again at the full record in light of this history.

## What I am requesting

I respectfully ask that Aetna:

1. Reverse the denial of hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) and approve this procedure, or
2. If additional clinical information or a peer-to-peer conversation between the plan's reviewer and Dr. Okafor would help resolve this, please let me know what is needed and I will work with my surgeon's office to provide it.

I have included [additional records if applicable, e.g., surgeon's letter, PT discharge note, imaging report — attach or list here] in support of this appeal.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-20. I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and I am also sending a copy by fax to 859-425-3379. I have confirmed [or will confirm] the correct appeal mailing address printed on my denial letter before mailing a paper copy, since that address is authoritative.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Foster**
Member ID: W492196775
[Address]

[Email address]
[Date]
